skipFiles.Aganorsa Leaf/mi-querida.json: Mi Querida is already a line under Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust (mi-querida, mi-querida-black, mi-querida-triqui-traca); not creating a duplicate brand
skipFiles.Charter Oak/charter-oak-connecticut-broa: Already on the site as Foundation's Charter Oak Broadleaf (same Toro 6x52); not creating a separate Charter Oak brand
skipFiles.Charter Oak/charter-oak-connecticut-shad: Already on the site as Foundation's Charter Oak line; only the missing Toro 6x52 was added to it by hand

brandStory.adventura: ADVentura is made and distributed by ADV & McKay Cigars Co., founded in 2016 by Henderson Ventura of Tabacalera William Ventura and Marcel Knobel, a Swiss sommelier and coffee producer-retailer. It sold in Europe from 2017 and reached the U.S. market around 2019 at the IPCPR trade show.
brandStory.asylum: Asylum was created in 2012 by Tom Lazuka, a former Camacho and Davidoff sales rep, together with Christian Eiroa, and is sold as its own brand rather than under the CLE name. Lazuka's pitch was oversized cigars of 60 to 80 ring gauge, which Eiroa reportedly dismissed as a bad idea before agreeing to make them at his factory in Danlí, Honduras. Its blends favor value and bold, full-flavored profiles in very large ring gauges.
brandStory.casa-de-garcia: Casa de Garcia is a budget, bundle-tier brand distributed by Altadis USA and sold mostly in bundles at roughly $1-2 per cigar. Its four core wrapper-variant lines are made in the Dominican Republic and its two Centenario lines in Nicaragua by the Plasencia family in Estelí. No founding year has been found.
brandStory.dbl: DBL stands for Dominican Big Leaguer, a baseball-themed boutique brand founded by Francisco Almonte and made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. Releases are documented from at least 2016 through 2026.
brandStory.deadwood-tobacco-co: Deadwood Tobacco Co. began as a South Dakota retail-exclusive brand and went national through Drew Estate around 2016, where it is rolled at La Gran Fabrica in Estelí, Nicaragua. Its four core blends are known as the Wild Bunch: Sweet Jane, Fat Bottom Betty, Crazy Alice and Leather Rose, joined in 2025 by a Dominicana sub-line.
brandStory.domain-cigars: Domain is an independent brand founded in March 2024 by Daniel Lance, who has a cigar-retail background, and Esteban Disla, a cigar maker with roughly ten years at Fabrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño and blends for CAO, Toraño and Alec Bradley. It operates as a full-service tobacco company covering agriculture, processing, brokering and cigar making in Estelí, Nicaragua.
brandStory.don-diego: Don Diego is currently distributed in the U.S. by Altadis USA. Retailers categorize it as Dominican-made; that origin and the brand's history have not been confirmed from a primary source.
brandStory.dos-amigos: Dos Amigos (1987) is a 2025 brand conceived in Barcelona by Jordi Llorens and Isidre Pineda, with its cigars produced in Nicaragua. It launched internationally at InterTabac 2025 and has been covered mainly by European trade press.
brandStory.gispert: Gispert is distributed by Altadis USA, which launched the Gispert Intenso line extension in 2017 as a collaboration with A.J. Fernandez. Retailers categorize it as Dominican-made; its founding history has not been confirmed.
brandStory.jfr: JFR stands for Just For Retailers: it was created in 2005 to be sold through brick-and-mortar retailers rather than big-box or online-only channels. Made in Estelí, Nicaragua, it has been associated with Casa Fernandez and is now attributed to Aganorsa Leaf as one of its best-selling house brands.
brandStory.las-cabrillas: Las Cabrillas is a long-running line named for New World explorers such as Balboa, De Soto, Cortez and Columbus. It is rolled in Honduras with all-Mexican San Andrés binder and filler, an unusual combination, and comes in Connecticut Shade natural and San Andrés maduro wrappers.
brandStory.omar-ortez: Omar Ortez is distributed by Altadis USA and remains active, with a new three-count fresh pack announced in 2025. Retailers and the Altadis product listing point to Honduran manufacture, though its founding year and history are unconfirmed.
brandStory.onyx: Onyx was founded in 2000 and named for its original near-black Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Now distributed and manufactured by Altadis USA, it has grown from a single Dominican maduro line into three lines spanning Dominican and Nicaraguan-puro blends.
brandStory.primo-del-rey: Primo del Rey cigars are handmade in Honduras according to current retailer listings. No founder, founding date or parent company has been found, and only a small number of retailers currently carry it.
brandStory.saint-luis-rey: This is the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey distributed by Altadis USA, which takes its name from a Cuban trademark registered in the 1940s and nationalized in 1960. The modern Honduran blend was created in 1996 by Christian Eiroa, later moved to Flor de Copán, and was reformulated as SLR Gen2 in 2013. It is positioned as accessible premium at roughly $6-9 per cigar.
brandStory.topper-cigar-company: Topper Cigar Company is an independent fourth-generation family business founded in 1896 in McSherrystown, Pennsylvania, and now run by Chris Topper. Its cigars are made in Danlí, Honduras, and it is unrelated to J.C. Newman.
brandStory.trinidad: This is the non-Cuban Trinidad distributed by Altadis USA, separate from the Cuban original that was created in 1969 at El Laguito in Havana as a diplomatic gift. Altadis relaunched the name around 2017 with Trinidad Santiago, driven by Rafael Nodal, and current lines are made in the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. The 1969 date is the Cuban original's founding year.
brandStory.bandolero: Bandolero was created by Nelson Alfonso, founder of Selected Tobacco S.A., and is distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars. Rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica, it is organized into three core series distinguished by wrapper shade, plus a newer premium line aged in Madrid, Spain.
brandStory.firecracker: Firecracker dates to 2007, when it was exclusive to Two Guys Smoke Shop in New Hampshire; United Cigars now distributes it nationwide. Its signature format is a 3.5 x 50 petite robusto with a pigtail cap resembling a fuse.
brandStory.garofalo: Garofalo La Famiglia was released by United Cigars, owned by David Garofalo, and named for his family. It is made by Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua, was announced in December 2021 and shipped to retailers in January 2022.
brandStory.gold-star: Gold Star was first introduced in 1995 and lay dormant for years before a 2024 limited-edition revival supporting the Navy SEAL Gold Star Program. It moved into full regular production in March 2025, with a wider rollout after the April 2025 PCA trade show.
brandStory.hightower: Hightower is marketed as JD Hightower by Jose Dominguez and made at the Magia Cubana factory in the Dominican Republic. Reviews date back to at least 2012, before United Cigars became involved.
brandStory.la-gianna-havana: La Gianna Havana is a United Cigars brand first released in 1994 and named to commemorate the birth of David Garofalo's daughter. It is handcrafted at Diadema Cigars de Honduras in Danlí, Honduras.
brandStory.montosa: Montosa is produced by Arnold André in the Dominican Republic from Cibao Valley tobaccos and distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars. The Montosa Maduro was named Cigar of the Year 2022 by The Cigar Authority.
brandStory.red-anchor: Red Anchor is a naval-rank-themed line distributed by United Cigars and made at the Kelner Boutique Factory. The Admiral was released in 2022, followed by the Captain, Commodore, Gunner and Cooper, announced at PCA 2023.
brandStory.terra-nova: Terra Nova is manufactured by Arnold André Dominicana in the Dominican Republic and has been distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars and Two Guys Cigars under a January 2022 deal.
brandStory.yaya: YaYa was created by Carlos Guillermo and launched in the Dominican Republic in 2019, with its U.S. debut through United Cigars at the PCA 2022 trade show. The name nods to a woman nicknamed Yaya who rolled her own blends.
brandStory.vegafina: VegaFina is named for its 1998 founding year and has historically been far stronger in Europe than in the U.S. The brand is owned by Tabacalera USA and distributed in the U.S. by Altadis USA; its production has been disrupted since 2025 by sanctions affecting its main factory.
brandStory.henry-clay: Henry Clay was founded in the 1840s in Cuba by Spanish immigrant Julian Alvarez Granda and named for the American statesman. After the Cuban original was nationalized, the U.S. trademark passed through Henry Clay & Bock Co. to Consolidated Cigar Corporation, which began making non-Cuban Henry Clays by 1986 and was later acquired by Altadis. Today's lines are made in several countries: the core line in the Dominican Republic, War Hawk in Honduras and War Hawk Rebellious in Nicaragua.
